scope.in: Part IV rent provisions: ss 27, 27AA, 28, 29 (so far as the bond turns on rent), 30, 31A, 31B, 31, 32; Part V provisions by which a tenancy ends and the next begins: ss 60, 64, 65, 70, 70A, 76C; s 26B (retaliatory action), to which s 64 points; the definitions in s 3 these provisions use; the Residential Tenancies Regulations 1989 so far as these provisions depend on them.
out: the rest of Part IV: Division 1A (ss 27A-27C: form of agreement, information for tenants, condition reports), ss 33-36 (receipts, payment and records of rent, apportionment), Division 2 (general standard terms: repairs, urgent repairs, quiet enjoyment, security, entry, outgoings, utilities, assignment), Divisions 2A and 2B (pets, modifications) and Division 3 (ss 51-59F) - none decides how much rent is payable, when it may rise, or when a tenancy ends and the next begins; where an in-scope provision reads one of them (s 29(1)(b)(ii) reads permission to keep a pet, s 26B(2)(a) reads requests for repairs) the reference register takes its result as a fact

termination on grounds in Part V: breach (s 62), sale (s 63), frustration (s 69), family violence (Division 2A, ss 71AA-71AF), social housing (Division 3, ss 71A-71J), court termination on grounds (ss 73A, 73, 74, 75A, 75), abandonment (ss 76A-78B), with the court-order routes (ss 71, 72) and holding over, abandoned goods and recovery (ss 76, 79-81B) - a separate scheme whose result s 60 reads as a fact (a notice given, an order made, the premises abandoned)

bond release and bond administration: Part 5A (ss 81C-81T), Schedule 1, and s 29(1)(a), (2A), (4)-(6) and (9) (single bond, instalments, receipt, lodgement and payment to the bond administrator) - they do not turn on rent; only the bond's maximum (s 29(1)(b), (2), (3)) and its increase (s 31) are in scope
Part VIA (residential tenancy databases, ss 82A-82K) - no in-scope provision refers to it

Parts I-III and VI except where an in-scope provision cross-refers to or depends on them - the reference register decides each one (encoded: ss 3A, 26A, 82, 85; facts: ss 5, 6, 7A, 12, 12A, 13, 84, 86B, 88C)

ss 61, 66, 67 and 68 (form of notices, acceptance of rent, tenant's notice without grounds) - not in the scope list; the reference register takes compliance with ss 61 and 67, and a tenant's notice under s 68, as facts

Part 7 (savings and transitional provisions) other than ss 99 and 100 - spent, or about provisions out of scope; ss 99-100 decide which version of ss 30 and 31A governs an agreement in force on 29 Jul 2024, so the reference register encodes them

the Residential Tenancies Regulations 1989 other than rr 5B, 5CA, 5CB, 7D, 7F, 7FA, 10AD, 10A, 11 and 12I - they serve provisions out of scope, or are spent (rr 7C and 7E apply only to fixed terms that expired by 31 Jul 2013); r 18 and Schedule 4 Form 1C are read only as the prescribed form for s 61, a fact
scope.why: The run asks how rent is set and varied under a residential tenancy agreement and how one tenancy ends and the next begins: the continuation rules (ss 31B, 70A, 76C), the no-ground termination (s 64) that the retaliatory-action provision (s 26B) now qualifies, and the bond so far as it follows the rent. Everything else in the Act is left out unless an in-scope provision reads it; then the reference register says whether it is encoded or taken as a fact. The 'in' statement and the first five areas of the 'out' list were set in the brief for this run; the last three (ss 61 and 66-68, Part 7, the Regulations) were added by the agent at 2A. The human approves or changes the scope at 3H.
